title: Landing pages and CRO
hired_for: To turn more of the visitors we already pay for into buyers, by making every page keep the ad's promise, answer the shopper's doubts, and prove each change with a real result.

jobs.job: Make the page keep the promise the ad made
jobs.why: When the ad says 3 for $30 and the page shows a different offer, or the guarantee disappears at checkout, shoppers feel tricked and leave. The ad money is spent and the sale is lost.

watch.metric: bounce rate on pages that paid social ads land on, mobile, 7 days
watch.source: GA4 by landing page and source

drives.metric: cost per purchase from paid social

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the top ad promises free shipping and the page does not mention it; bounce is 71%. After: the offer, price and guarantee match; bounce falls to 58% within 14 days.
jobs.who_today: media buyer and designer, rarely checked together

jobs.job: Fix the first screen of the product page on a phone
jobs.why: Most shoppers are on a phone and many never scroll. If price, proof, the size picker and the buy button are not all on the first screen, they leave without deciding.

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, mobile, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now reviews and delivery time sit below the fold and mobile add to cart is 6.1%. After: all 5 first screen items visible; add to cart 7.4%.

jobs.job: Find the one step where most shoppers drop and fix that first
jobs.why: Fixing everything at once wastes months. The step that loses the most buyers, weighted by value, is where the next dollar of work pays back most.

watch.metric: step rates: product view to cart, cart to checkout, checkout to order, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now cart to checkout is 38%, far below the other steps. After: fixed first; cart to checkout 46% in 30 days.

jobs.job: Stop popups and chat widgets from covering the buy button on phones
jobs.why: A popup that fires in the first 3 seconds or a chat bubble over the add to cart button blocks the one thing we want the shopper to do. It is a quick fix with an instant effect.

watch.metric: mobile add to cart rate on pages with a popup or widget, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the email popup fires at 2 seconds and covers the button. After: it waits for exit intent; mobile add to cart up from 5.8% to 6.4%.
jobs.who_today: nobody; each app is set up alone

jobs.job: Show the full cost and delivery date before checkout so no one quits at the last step
jobs.why: Surprise shipping costs and unknown delivery dates are the top reasons shoppers leave at checkout. Showing them early removes the surprise.

watch.metric: checkout abandonment at the shipping step, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 29% of checkouts stop at the shipping step. After: cost and date shown on the product page and cart; 21%.

jobs.job: Send each ad to the right kind of page for how much the shopper already knows
jobs.why: A cold shopper who has never heard of the brand needs a story or a quiz before a product page. A returning shopper wants the product page and the buy button.

watch.metric: conversion rate by landing page type for cold paid traffic, 30 days
watch.source: GA4 by landing page and campaign

jobs.now_after: Example: Now all cold ads land on the home page, converting at 0.9%. After: split between product pages and 1 story page; 1.4%.

jobs.job: Put proof right next to the doubt it answers
jobs.why: Reviews stacked at the bottom do not help the shopper who doubts the fit at the size picker. Proof works where the doubt happens.

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now all 3 proof blocks sit at the bottom and 4 top doubts have no proof near them. After: each doubt has proof beside it; add to cart up 0.6 points.

jobs.job: Answer the top reason people almost did not buy, in their own words
jobs.why: The same 3 or 4 doubts show up in tickets, reviews and surveys. When the page answers them in the customer's words, fewer people write in and more people buy.

watch.metric: questions asked before buying, tickets per 1,000 product page sessions, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 'will it fit wide feet' drives 1 in 4 pre-sale tickets and the page does not answer it. After: answered near the size picker; those tickets fall by half.
jobs.who_today: customer service and copywriter, not talking to each other

jobs.job: Show bundle and multi-pack savings in dollars so more shoppers buy more
jobs.why: 'Save 15%' means little. 'Save $12' next to a clear best-value pack moves shoppers up a tier and lifts profit per order.

watch.metric: units per order and average order value, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 18% of orders take a multi-pack. After: savings shown in dollars with 3 tiers; 26%, average order value up $6.

jobs.job: Make the cart raise order value without slowing checkout
jobs.why: A free shipping bar or one relevant add-on in the cart can lift the order value. Too many extras make shoppers hesitate and leave.

watch.metric: average order value and cart to checkout rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no free shipping bar and average order value is $38. After: bar set at $50 plus 1 add-on; $43 with cart to checkout held.
jobs.who_today: theme default or an upsell app

jobs.job: Judge pages by money per visitor, not conversion rate alone
jobs.why: A page can convert more and earn less if it pushes cheap items or deep discounts. Profit per visitor is the number that pays the bills.

watch.metric: revenue per visitor and gross profit per visitor, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the team reports conversion rate only; a 20% off test 'won' but cut profit per visitor by $0.30. After: every page read on profit per visitor.

jobs.job: Cut distractions on single offer pages
jobs.why: Full menus, competing offers and links to the blog pull the shopper away from the one thing we want them to do.

watch.metric: click through from the landing page to product or checkout, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now the campaign page shows the full menu and 3 offers; 34% click through. After: logo, cart and 1 button; 45%.

jobs.job: Check every page works on the phones our customers use before sending traffic
jobs.why: A page built on a desktop screen often breaks on a phone: text too small, buttons hidden, forms too long. Most paid traffic arrives on phones.

watch.metric: gap between mobile and desktop conversion rate, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now mobile converts at 1.1% and desktop at 2.6%. After: gap cut by a third within 60 days.

jobs.job: Only call a test a winner when the result is real
jobs.why: Tests stopped early, split unevenly or run over a sale weekend produce winners that fade. Rolling out a false winner can lower sales.

watch.metric: tests called only after the planned sample, full weeks and an even split, share
watch.source: brand brain experiment log and test tool export

drives.metric: shipped winners that still hold their lift after 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 3 of the last 5 wins were called in under a week. After: all calls follow the plan; 4 of 5 winners hold.

jobs.job: Help shoppers pick the right size so fewer orders come back
jobs.why: Wrong size is the top return reason for socks, shoes and clothing. A clear size guide next to the picker saves the return and the reship.

watch.metric: returns for size or fit, share of orders, 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 5.2% of orders come back for fit. After: size guide by the picker; 3.8% in 60 days.

jobs.job: Keep urgency and low stock messages true
jobs.why: A countdown that resets or a 'only 3 left' that never changes teaches shoppers not to trust anything on the page. It can also break consumer law.

watch.metric: pages with a stock or countdown message that does not match real stock or promo end, count
watch.source: brand brain page check against Shopify inventory

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 pages show a countdown that restarts every visit. After: 0; stock messages read live inventory.

jobs.job: Rank the test ideas by the money they could make, not by opinion
jobs.why: The loudest idea often gets tested first. Ranking by expected profit and evidence means the next test is the one most likely to pay.

watch.metric: test ideas with a profit estimate and at least 2 pieces of evidence, share

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 30 ideas in the list, 4 with evidence. After: 30 scored; the top 5 each worth an estimated $2,000 or more a month.

jobs.job: Decide when to skip the test and just ship the fix
jobs.why: A broken button or a missing price does not need a test. Small stores without enough traffic should ship clear fixes and save tests for real questions.

watch.metric: days from finding a clear fix to shipping it

jobs.now_after: Example: Now a broken size picker waited 3 weeks for a test slot. After: clear fixes ship within 3 days.

jobs.job: Make site search turn searches into sales
jobs.why: Shoppers who search are ready to buy. When search returns nothing or the wrong product, they leave.

watch.metric: searches with no results, share, and conversion rate of sessions that search, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 14% of searches return nothing, including 'wool'. After: synonyms added; under 4%.

jobs.job: Set up every test so it tracks in both versions and the page does not flicker
jobs.why: A test that does not track in one version, or flashes the old page on a slow phone, wastes weeks and gives a false answer.

watch.metric: tests restarted or thrown out for a setup fault, count per quarter

drives.metric: tests that give a usable answer

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 2 of 6 tests last quarter were thrown out. After: 0 of 6, with a real device check before launch.

jobs.job: Make the home and collection pages move shoppers to the right product fast
jobs.why: The home page is a hallway, not a shop counter. If shoppers cannot reach the right product in 2 taps, they leave.

watch.metric: sessions that view a product page, share of sessions starting on home or collection pages, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 41% of home page visits reach a product. After: best sellers and clear paths up top; 52%.

jobs.job: Hear why buyers bought and why others left
jobs.why: Surveys and short calls tell the team what the numbers cannot: the real doubt, the words customers use, and what almost stopped them.

watch.metric: post purchase and exit survey answers collected, count per month
watch.source: Shopify post purchase survey and Klaviyo

drives.metric: test ideas backed by customer evidence

jobs.now_after: Example: Now no survey runs. After: 200 answers a month; top 3 doubts feed the test list.

jobs.job: Give returning customers a fast way to buy again
jobs.why: A repeat buyer knows what they want. Making them go through the full story page wastes their time and some give up.

watch.metric: conversion rate of returning customers, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now returning customers convert at 4.2% after a 5 step path. After: a 2 tap reorder link in emails; 5.5%.

jobs.job: Check a winner's returns and repeat orders before rolling it out for good
jobs.why: A page that sells harder can bring buyers who return more or never come back. The real win shows 60 days later.

watch.metric: 60 day return rate and repeat rate, winner group against control group

jobs.now_after: Example: Now winners are shipped and never checked. After: each checked at 60 days; 1 of 4 rolled back for higher returns.

jobs.job: Keep story pages and quizzes honest: labeled as ads, real reviews, no invented experts
jobs.why: A made up expert or review can get ads banned and invite legal trouble. It also breaks trust the moment a shopper checks.

watch.metric: live pages with an unverified claim, review or endorsement, count
watch.source: brand brain claims and proof checked against site pages

drives.metric: ads rejected by Meta for landing page issues, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now 1 story page quotes a doctor with no record on file. After: 0 unverified items on live pages.
